own_solution.law: Doppler effect in still air, applied twice: lorry panel as receding observer f1 = f (v - u)/v, then as receding source f2 = f1 v/(v + u); recorder as observer moving with the sound (away from the lorry) f3 = f2 (v - w)/v. Shift = f - f3 = f [1 - (v - u)(v - w)/(v (v + u))].
assumptions: speeds below the speed of sound

notes: v = 343, u = 6, w = 9: f3 = 1500 * 337 * 334 / (349 * 343) = 1500 * 112558/119707 = 1410.419 Hz, shift 89.581 Hz. With the recorder carried at 1.6 m/s relative to the trolley deck (ground speed 10.6 m/s away from the lorry): f3 = 1500 * 337 * 332.4 / 119707 = 1403.662 Hz, shift 96.338 Hz. The 82 m distance sets arrival time but cancels from the steady-state frequency (it enters a wavefront-timing derivation and drops out), so C; it could arguably be called D since it does not appear in the Doppler formula. Toolbox-carrying and earlier-run sentences have no path to the recorder's speed now. All 1.6 m/s sentences state 1.6 m/s; walking-pace sentences are numeral-free; both 82 m sentences match. I read 1.6 m/s as relative to the deck, the natural reading of 'walks along its deck'.
